method: read-only official GitHub plugin fetch_file/fetch calls; no reproduction or training

optimizer.scope: all model parameters, including image encoder and text decoder; not last-layer LoRA

derived_training_scale.gradient_accumulation: not configured in Trainer; standard default 1
derived_training_scale.evidence_type: derived from published recipe, not independently measured optimizer log

reported_test.evidence_type: author-reported example for the documented CORD recipe
reported_test.short_original_excerpt: Total number of samples: 100, Tree Edit Distance (TED) based accuracy score: 0.9129639764131697, F1 accuracy score: 0.8406020841373987

training_targets.loss: next-token cross entropy; input shifted by one against labels

limitations: The model generates custom key boundary tokens such as <s_menu> and </s_menu>, then token2json constructs a JSON object; it does not directly generate literal brace-and-quote JSON.
The reported 91.3 percent is tree edit accuracy, not JSON syntax validity, complete protocol success, or native EOS rate.
The inference code strips EOS and padding before parsing; the official report does not separately quantify native EOS termination success.

Donut is pretrained for document reading and uses full encoder-decoder parameter updates; the current RM65-B pilot starts from action SFT weights and updates only last-layer q/o LoRA. Its sample efficiency is not a guarantee for the RM65-B setup.
The hundreds or thousands of downstream receipt samples must be distinguished from the millions of examples used to pretrain the document model.
OCR/document extraction is not robot perception, memory-dependent role binding, executability, or task success.
